slice.leaf: Determine whether GitHub immutable releases provide a provider-enforced append-only, directly Chat-readable monotonic rollback witness without new admin/rules setup, manual attestation, external storage/compute, finite monthly quota, or added cost.
slice.candidate: GitHub immutable releases with locked tag/assets and automatic release attestation

sources.observed: After publication, immutable-release assets cannot be modified or deleted and the associated tag cannot be moved or deleted while the release exists. If the immutable release is deleted, the tag may then be deleted, although the same tag name cannot be reused. Repository-resurrection reuse of those tag names is also blocked.
Release immutability must be enabled at repository or organization settings and applies only to future releases.
Checking whether immutable releases are enabled requires Administration read permission; enabling or disabling them requires Administration write permission.
GitHub documents verification of an immutable release through GitHub CLI or the web UI.
Published releases can be listed/read through the Releases REST API, while release management APIs include deletion.

observations: The tag and release assets are provider-locked after publication, which is stronger than an ordinary mutable ref for rewrite resistance.
The immutable release object itself is not documented as undeletable: GitHub explicitly describes deletion of an immutable release, after which its tag can also be deleted.

GitHub documents a persistent no-reuse rule for the old tag name, including repository-resurrection protection, but the reviewed public docs do not expose a normal public read endpoint that enumerates deleted-release/tag-name tombstones as durable witness state.
Repository-level enablement and enablement-status inspection require Administration permissions, so the mechanism is not a generic no-new-admin-prerequisite primitive.
Automatic release attestations reduce manual-attestation dependency, but this slice did not establish an independently retained Chat-readable attestation record that survives release deletion.
inferences: Immutable releases are a strong anti-rewrite component but fail the stricter monotonic-witness threat model because the readable release can be deleted and the surviving no-reuse property is not documented as directly readable historical state after deletion.

Even if a repository already has immutability enabled, acceptance cannot generalize to the required generic mechanism without proving deletion-surviving readback. Requiring an administrator to enable or inspect the feature would violate the tested no-new-admin-prerequisite scope.

slice.result_reason: Immutable releases materially strengthen anti-rewrite guarantees for tag/assets, but the release can be deleted, deletion-surviving tombstone history is not documented as directly Chat-readable, and generic use requires repository/organization Administration setup or inspection. Therefore the candidate does not satisfy the exact no-admin, provider-retained, directly readable monotonic-witness threat model.
slice.tested_scope: Official GitHub immutable-release concepts, enablement, verification and REST release/repository documentation only; no O/downstream/other-worker semantics, no repository mutation outside cross_field role-local state/receipt, no release creation/deletion experiment, no admin/rules change, no webhook/external storage, no hosted compute/storage, no external execution, no manual attestation, no finite monthly/trial/paid quota, no added cost, no scheduler mutation, no same-run retry, and no second semantic leaf.
slice.conflict_check: Only cross_field role-local checkpoint/LATEST and immutable own receipt namespaces are authorized for this slice.

frontier: Preserve r273 single-ref immutable transaction-record plus force=false ref-update design as the current Chat-callable baseline.
r276 rejected GitHub Events API as a durable monotonic witness because visibility is bounded and not real-time.

r277 rejects immutable releases as the complete witness: tag/assets are locked, but the release can be deleted; the surviving tag-name no-reuse rule lacks documented normal public tombstone readback; enablement/status also requires Administration authority.

Automatic release attestations remain a potentially useful subcomponent only if a future slice proves an independently retained, directly Chat-readable transparency record that survives release deletion without admin setup, hosted execution/storage, finite quota, or added cost.
